items.name: Latent Lattice Language Models
items.title: Latent Lattice Language Models
items.description: Language models typically increase per-token computation through deeper or looped layers and latent reasoning steps, while richer residual connections improve information flow across layers. We instead increase computational capacity: the number of active computational states a model maintains. items.name: ViRA: Toward Ultra-High-Resolution Visual Agents via Cross-Input Relative Policy Optimization
items.title: ViRA: Toward Ultra-High-Resolution Visual Agents via Cross-Input Relative Policy Optimization
items.description: Visual agents answer questions about ultra-high-resolution photos by zooming into the relevant regions. However, existing agents often answer from common sense instead of reading the evidence. Reinforcement learning (RL) on the final answer cannot correct this, because a guess earns the same reward as reading. items.title: Quantifying the added value of human forecaster discussions for tropical cyclone intensity prediction
items.description: The National Hurricane Center routinely releases Tropical Cyclone Discussions that offer insights into its tropical cyclone forecasts. This study examines the added value of these discussions for intensity forecasting beyond a set of numerical predictors. items.name: How VLMs Plan What's Next
items.title: How VLMs Plan What's Next
items.description: When a vision-language model describes an image, it names one object at a time and it rarely repeats itself, yet how the model plans this order is far from obvious. We characterize the mechanism a VLM uses to decide where to look before it looks. The mechanism has four main parts. First, binding heads match the relevant text tokens against the image and resolve them into pointers to the matched image region. items.title: Mitigating Catastrophic Forgetting with Physics-Indexed Specialist Memory: the Evolutionary Neuroplastic Agent

items.name: Optimal Autoregressive Chain-of-Thought Learning via Bagging

items.description: We study how to learn an autoregressive next-token generator $f\colonΣ^\star\toΣ$ from a class $\mathcal{F}$, given chain-of-thought (CoT) demonstrations of length $T$ generated by $f$. items.title: SADL: On the Demand-Supply Geometry of Representation Collapse
items.description: In Joint-Embedding Predictive Architectures (JEPAs), a well-constrained projector output does not by itself prevent representation collapse. We find that, from initialization, the encoder representation is dominated by a component shared by different inputs. items.title: Surrogate-Assisted Compact-Model Extraction for SKY130 CMOS at 77 K
items.description: Cryogenic circuit design requires compact transistor models that reproduce measured low-temperature behavior and run in standard circuit simulators. We fit BSIM4 parameters to measured I-V curves of SkyWater 130 nm (SKY130) transistors at 77 K using a neural surrogate of NGSpice. items.name: Beyond Job Titles: Interpreting Early-Career Job Advertisements with Sparse Autoencoders and Semantic Clustering
items.title: Beyond Job Titles: Interpreting Early-Career Job Advertisements with Sparse Autoencoders and Semantic Clustering
items.description: Job titles and job descriptions alone provide limited insight into how technical roles differ in a changing job market. To assess how such roles differ in their work and industry applications, we design and compare two methods based on deep learning and transformer representations using 36,081 early-career job postings collected from LinkedIn in the United States between December 2025 and October 2026. These differences complicate debugging and training audits and can cause training and inference engines to disagree. items.description: Cyber-range and capture-the-flag scenario construction remains labor-intensive because authors must coordinate infrastructure, vulnerable services, attack paths, artifacts, and success conditions. items.title: When Tool Names Are Not Identities: Measuring Provider Misbinding in MCP-Based AI Agents
items.description: Large language model (LLM) applications increasingly act as agents that select and invoke external tools. The Model Context Protocol (MCP) standardizes this interaction by allowing clients to compose tools advertised by multiple servers. items.title: DynSurvX: Time-Resolved Explanations for Dynamic Survival Predictions
items.description: Recent survival models integrating longitudinal data achieve strong predictive performance, but their predictions are often difficult to interpret, limiting their clinical use. We propose DynSurvX, a model-agnostic explainability framework for dynamic survival prediction with mixed static and longitudinal covariates. items.title: When Do Histology Foundation Models Need Geometric Test-Time Augmentation?
items.description: Test-time augmentation (TTA) aggregates model predictions across multiple transformed views of an input during inference. items.title: Reading or Remembering? Measuring Temporal Contamination in Language Models
items.description: Language models are now used to read central-bank text for economic forecasting, but most were trained on text written after the documents they read. items.title: Benchmarking memory and nonlinear processing capacity of quantum recurrent neural networks for time series prediction
items.description: Quantum machine learning has emerged as a promising approach to time series prediction. While quantum reservoir computing has been widely explored for this setting, variational quantum models tailored to sequential data remain comparatively understudied, largely because they are difficult to train. items.title: ONAM: Fitting Orthogonal Neural Additive Models for Post-Hoc Interpretability of Black-Box Predictions
items.description: Modern machine learning models, such as artificial neural networks, achieve high predictive performance through increasingly complex black-box architectures, limiting their use in settings where transparency, interpretability, and fairness are required. items.title: TRACE: Topological Representations for Anomaly detection through Contrastive Embeddings
items.description: Intrusion detectors must recognize evolving malicious behavior even when confirmed attack labels are scarce or incomplete. We present TRACE, a topology-aware graph contrastive learning framework for label-efficient intrusion detection. items.title: Right Reason, Wrong Advice: Evaluating Recourse in LLM Explanations of Denied Requests

items.title: SciResearch-Eval: Evaluating Scientific Judgment in Autonomous Experimental Agents
items.description: We introduce SciResearch-Eval, an interactive benchmark of scientific judgment built on a standard laboratory problem: measuring a material's thermal properties by heating it and fitting a heat-conduction simulator.
